title: Error Handling Patterns Consistency Review
scope: Error handling patterns, silent failures, error propagation across engines and dispatchers

return_format.structure: { content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(error) }], isError: true }

silent_failure_analysis.assessment: LOW RISK - most are intentional fire-and-forget patterns
recommendations: Add comment explaining why catch is empty
Consider using void operator: void promise.catch(() => {})

error_propagation_patterns.assessment: GOOD - most errors propagate to caller

inconsistencies_identified.description: Some engines return { error: ... }, others return { success: false, error: ... }, others throw
inconsistencies_identified.recommendation: Document expected pattern per engine category
Add log.error calls in catch blocks for observability

inconsistencies_identified.description: 16 empty catches lack comments explaining intent

safety_critical.pattern: throw on validation failure, return detailed error

calculation.pattern: Return { result, confidence, warnings } with edge case handling

data_access.pattern: Return null/empty on not found, throw on corruption
data_access.log_level: info for not found, error for corruption

strengths: dispatcherError() provides consistent MCP-compliant error format (100% adoption)
1127 throw statements indicate explicit error signaling
93.9% error propagation rate - errors reach callers
Low silent failure count (16 of 1969 catch blocks = 0.8%)
concerns: Multiple error return formats in engines (not standardized)
Empty catches lack documentation of intent
recommendations: Create EngineError base class for consistent engine errors
Add telemetry for error tracking in production
Document expected error handling pattern in CLAUDE.md
Add linting rule to flag undocumented empty catches
